quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: Which option gives a rider the best protection?
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield and eyeglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids while braking, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake immediately and apply it smoothly again.

questions.question: If you shift into a lower gear without going slow enough, the:

options.text: Motorcycle could jerk forward and the rear tire could skid.
Engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle could jerk forward and the rear tire could skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift into a lower gear without going slow enough, the motorcycle will jerk forward and the rear tire may skid.

questions.question: When braking on surfaces with poor grip, you should:
questions.explanation: On surfaces with poor grip, apply the brakes gently to slow or stop safely.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle with a sidecar, where should the passenger sit?

options.text: Either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Neither on the motorcycle nor in the sidecar.

questions.explanation: A passenger should ride in the sidecar and keep both hands inside at all times.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You may pass in a no-passing zone.
You may go 10 mph over the speed limit to complete the pass.
You must start and finish the pass in a legal passing zone.
You must complete the pass on the shoulder if one exists.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a legal passing zone.
questions.explanation: Passing must happen only in areas where it is legal and safe, at or below the speed limit.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping, you should use both brakes:
questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the best stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert riders about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Push the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
Push the handlebar grip opposite the direction you want to turn.
Not hold the grip because it is dangerous.
Not lean the motorcycle as it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When going faster than walking speed, push the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn. This makes the motorcycle lean the right way.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Always wear reflective and bright clothing when riding. Crashes happen during the day and at night, so stay visible at all times.

questions.question: What can you do to be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to get attention.

questions.explanation: Use your headlight and position your motorcycle in the lane where oncoming traffic can see you best. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: If your motorcycle begins to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up to escape the wobble.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, slowly close the throttle to slow down, and lean your weight forward and down. Pull over as soon as possible.

questions.question: An effective face shield should NOT:
questions.explanation: A good face shield must be scratch-free, clear on the sides, tight-fitting, and allow air to flow through. Air flow is important because a sealed shield causes fogging, which blocks your vision.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is usually to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to move to another lane and let the tailgater pass you. Speeding up can make the danger worse.

questions.question: It is most important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: There is a stop sign ahead.
Your turn signals do not work.

questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is small and not as noticeable as a car's brake lights. Flash your brake light when you need to slow down quickly so other drivers will notice you.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, it is best to:

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.

questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and motorcycles with sidecars turn differently than two-wheeled motorcycles. You may need to move from the outside to the inside of a curve. Adjust your path based on how the vehicle handles.

questions.question: Approved helmets:

options.text: Allow you to see everything you need to see to the sides.
Do not have to be worn if you think they limit your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow you to see everything you need to see to the sides.
questions.explanation: Approved helmets do not limit vision in a dangerous way. They let you see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks that cross your lane at an angle, it is usually safest to:

options.text: Ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
Turn to avoid riding straight across.
Cross on the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: Cross the tracks while riding straight in your lane. Do not turn to cross at a 90-degree angle, as you could end up in another lane of traffic.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should NOT:
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed, avoid sudden movements, and brake slowly using both brakes.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Slow down, approach the dog, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, approach the dog, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Downshift and slowly approach the dog. Once you get close, accelerate to leave it behind. Do not try to kick the dog.
